I have been farming my six mu of land here in Quzhou for over thirty years, and I know what this soil and climate can do. Around here, the only sensible system is winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same plots. That is what I will do this year.

My wheat went into the ground last October after rotary tillage, using an improved variety that has done well for me before. It is already up and growing. In the coming weeks I will top-dress it with urea and give it two more irrigations, for a total of three this season. I also spray four times — herbicide once and fungicide or insecticide as needed — to keep the crop clean. I expect about 500 kg per mu at harvest in early June if the weather holds.

The day we finish cutting the wheat, I will sow hybrid maize directly into the wheat stubble with no-tillage. There is no time to waste between crops, and leaving the stubble on the field saves water and keeps the soil from drying out. The maize will get less nitrogen than the wheat — it does not need as much — and I will irrigate it twice over the summer. I will spray four times for weeds and pests. If all goes well, I should get about 550 kg per mu of maize by October.

I do not grow cotton or vegetables. They bring more risk and take more labor than my wife and I can handle at our age, and the grain market is steady.
